questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a university that offers courses in intellectual property law. Furthermore, I wanted to study in a state with great weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is one of the greatest experiences of my life. So much fun to study at another university and travel on the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the information was easy to access on the University of Copenhagen's website but honestly, some information was missing, but I was lucky that I knew former exchange students to ask about some of the crucial information e.g., about housing, car renting, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of San Diego School of Law was great at providing us with the information we needed. The university arranged many good gatherings with the other exchange students at the university, so we could ask the other students about the city, housing, car renting, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy but I asked former exchange students and they provided me with the name of a landlord on Mission Beach which I contacted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will need a car!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Find housing before arriving! Look on Airbnb, ask former exchange students or current exchange students, etc.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Take the TOEFL test, apply by writing an application on the host university's website, get accepted, apply for a visa.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was guidance on the host university's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. All the courses I applied for, I got.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register in good time. If you have questions about anything, email your own university and the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was very high. Especially the finals were tough.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The form of teaching at The University of San Diego School of Law (and many other universities in the US) is based on The Socratic method (active learning), which means that most of the teaching is based on an argument-based dialogue between the teacher and the students. This form of teaching is particularly motivating because it requires students to prepare before the seminars and actively participate in the teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to US law
Negotiation
Intellectual property survey
International contracts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiation was a very giving course because it is universal which means you can use what you learn in many cases and in your daily life. It is a very active course, not so much reading assigned, and there is no final exam but more like a project where you have to show what you have learned.

questions.answer: The money spend on trips added up.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food (grocery shopping) and housing are very expensive in San Diego.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university arranged many gatherings with all the exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can register for many sports courses (80 dollars for a whole semester).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on as many trips as you can. Yosemite National Park was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough. Remember to give tips (at least 15% to the waiters, etc.).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I didn't socialize with local students as much as I wanted to. Go out, meet new people, ask your classmates for advice, etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I donøt think I found any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and friendliness when you meet the local people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Find housing before you arrive.
2) Rent a car at "Dirt Cheap Car Rental".
3) Participate as much as you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: USD has something going on almost every day (activities, free food, etc.), and remember to explore campus!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students, going on trips, and the courses were also very giving.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being out of my comfort zone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
